uncited: Physics and Optical Modeling extends the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representation to handle non-vacuum media and physically consistent surface extraction by modifying the rendering equation or the underlying density field.
It solves the problem of light transport in scattering media (e.g., underwater fog) and the geometric inconsistency of discrete alpha-blending for surface reconstruction.

Unlike [Color and Appearance Modeling](14740-color-and-appearance-modeling.md), which focuses on view-dependent shading and material properties in clear space, this family explicitly models volumetric attenuation and backscatter or reformulates the Gaussian primitive as a continuous attenuation field.
All methods in this family operate on the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting representation, where the scene is defined by a set of $N$ 3D Gaussians $\{G_i\}_{i=1}^N$.

Each Gaussian $G_i$ is defined by its mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}_i$, covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ (derived from rotation $\mathbf{R}_i$ and scale $\mathbf{S}_i$), opacity $\alpha_i$, and view-dependent color $\mathbf{c}_i(\omega)$.
The rendering process evaluates the Gaussian density along a ray $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o} + t\omega$ and integrates contributions.
The core variation across methods lies in the definition, storage, and optimization of $\mathbf{c}_i(\omega)$ and potentially $\alpha_i$, moving beyond the fixed SH coefficients used in base 3DGS.
**Post-Processing Transformation:** Applying a learned affine transformation to the rendered image based on 3D position and view embedding [14740-color-and-appearance-modeling.md].
**Factorized Illumination:** Separating scene lighting (via a tensor grid) from material properties (via BRDF features) to model specular effects [14740-color-and-appearance-modeling.md].

**Image-Conditioned Modulation:** Using an MLP and per-image embeddings to modulate Gaussian color and opacity, enabling transient object removal and appearance synthesis [14740-color-and-appearance-modeling.md].
**Neural Field Substitution:** Replacing per-Gaussian SH with a shared grid-based neural field to reduce parameters and improve generalization [14740-color-and-appearance-modeling.md].

**Volumetric Attenuation:** Modifying the alpha-blending equation to incorporate medium properties, such as direct attenuation $B_d$ and backscatter parameters $B_\infty, B_b$, to model light transport in non-vacuum media [15148-physics-and-optical-modeling.md].
The camera sensor must have a linear response to light.

The continuous attenuation model was introduced to address the geometric inconsistencies of discrete Gaussian splatting for surface extraction, leveraging theoretical results from Orienting Attenuation (OaV) [9624-continuous-attenuation-model-for-3d-gaussian-splatting.md].

Underwater 3D Gaussian Splatting (Gaussian Splashing) was developed to extend 3DGS to aquatic environments by incorporating ocean optics models, specifically addressing the limitations of vanilla 3DGS in handling distance-dependent attenuation and color casts [13980-underwater-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-backscatter-loss.md].
